chapter: Picnics, wagon advertising and saloon work
title: Lake picnics and pavilions
summary: He describes train rides to lakeside pavilions, hours played, clubs that sponsored picnics, basket picnics and the Eastman Farm.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Well, tell us about these picnics. I never did go to hardly any picnics. And they were out at the lake or her.
Oh, yeah, out at the lake. Gee, uh.
Near Millenburg or West End? Yeah, out Millenburg.
Out West End. Could you describe a picnic to us? Could you describe a picnic scene?
Because I danced. Oh, yeah. You see the picnics. After we had entered the train at Esplanade Street. Go out. Go out to the pavilion.
It was out.
Fully about a block.

Then the, uh, the, uh, what do you call it? The, uh, little pavilion. Yes, little pavilion and the band would play in there. See, they had each side gallery, they danced on the gallery. We played from nine.
Nine in the morning? Nine in the morning. Yes.
And we'd knock off recess at twelve. They had an hour recess while they'd eat. Then we'd come back and we'd eat lunch. And we'd start from about, say, about one to six.
Who would promote these picnics?
Oh, well, they had different clubs.
Clubs?
Right, different clubs.
Now, would a pavilion like that look like Mamalu's, or would it be different?
Well, it would be like on the order of Mamalu's, on that order. Set out on the water. Oh, gee, they had dozens of them.
But didn't you play outdoors, too? Didn't you play outdoors, also? Like on the lawn? You mean on picnic grounds? Yes, picnic grounds.
Oh, yes, I have played. I have played picnic grounds. Like out, uh, Millenburg. Basket picnic, you know what I'm saying?
Yep, everybody brought his own basket.
Yeah, brought their baskets.
What did they serve there? Did they have drinks and so on? Oh, yeah, beer.
Or did you bring your own? No, I guess they brought their little stuff. You know what I mean? But they'd have beer and soft drinks.
At the grounds.
Yeah. But then each one would carry their baskets.
For lunch.

That's right. Now, we play another place, very regular. It was a place called Eastman Farm. They give a lot of picnics. Every Sunday, we'd hire different bands. Where was that? That was back of Carlton.
Is that existing today or the high of the world? No, it's not.
